analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-use-after-free caused by deleting a multiply-inherited GPU resource object through a non-canonical base pointer (`GrGpuResource*`) in `GrGpuResource::CacheAccess::release()`. For `GrMockTextureRenderTarget` (inherits both `GrMockTexture` and `GrMockRenderTarget`, each deriving from `GrGpuResource`), one `GrGpuResource` subobject is released and then `delete fResource` frees the allocation. The resource still exists in cache containers via another `GrGpuResource` base/subobject entry, so `GrResourceCache::releaseAll()` later calls `release()` again on a dangling pointer, leading to UAF in `GrGpuResource::release()` (read at line 52).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the `api_mock_gpu_canvas` harness, fuzzed drawing commands create a renderable mock texture (`GrMockTextureRenderTarget`) via `GrMockGpu::onCreateTexture`. During context teardown (`GrDirectContext` -> `GrResourceCache::releaseAll()`), cache iterates nonpurgeable/purgeable resources and invokes `cacheAccess().release()` on stale entries. Because the same underlying object is represented through multiple `GrGpuResource` base paths (diamond/multiple inheritance) and one path already triggered `delete`, a subsequent release attempts to use freed memory. Trigger requires creation of this mock texture-render-target resource and teardown path that drains cache.
